text:
Rafael Mendes: Canary check-in for overload protection (us-east, 2 models) — can someone drop the latest shed rate + latency deltas? Also: did any customers actually see the new 429 behavior yet?

Aisha Bello: Dashboard here (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/overload-canary/us-east-canary
Quick summary last 24h:
- Shed rate (edge-admission + runtime sheds combined): avg 0.6%, peak 6.9% during the 18:00–18:20 UTC spike
- p99 latency: down ~28% vs baseline for same traffic shape (2.7s -> 1.95s)
- 5xx timeouts: basically gone during the spike window; mostly clean 429/503 w/ Retry-After

Sergio Costa: Adding breakdown by status:
- 429 share went from ~0.02% (mostly quota) to 0.4% overall; during spike it peaked at 3.1%
- 503 share peaked at 0.9% but with consistent body + Retry-After
- 502/504 basically zero, which is the big win (before canary we’d get gateway timeouts)
Also breaker state transitions look stable (no rapid open/close). :thumbsup:

Christine Wong: Re: breaker stability — I’m not seeing flapping on the new cooldown logic.
Open -> half-open -> closed transitions are happening on the order of minutes, not seconds.
Largest event:
- breaker opened for (model=rwi-chat-1, tier=free, region=us-east) at ~18:03 UTC
- stayed open ~7m
- half-open allowed 5% probes, recovered, then closed.

Tomáš Novák: Comparing to last month’s similar spike, this would have been a Sev2 (tail latency collapse + control plane lag). This time control plane p99 stayed under 120ms.
Queue depth stayed capped at the runtime boundary (no runaway), so we didn’t get the “everything is slow forever” failure mode.

Amara Diallo: On the gateway side, the admission hook is doing what we want.
We’re shedding earlier for requests that would have sat in queue >10s.
Headers present:
- Retry-After: mostly 2–5 seconds (saw a few 10s)
- x-redwood-overload-reason: `edge_admission`
No weird 500s from the middleware.

Rafael Mendes: Nice. Any reports from support / customer tickets triggered by 429s? I’m worried folks will interpret as rate limiting.

Aisha Bello: I checked the #support escalation channel earlier — no new threads explicitly tied to the canary. (Yet.)
We did see a small increase in “why am I getting 429” in logs from a few SDK user agents, but not linked to a ticket.

Mina Haddad: Routing perspective: most of the 429s are tier-aware (free got hit hardest). Paid tiers mostly saw 503 with fallback attempts, then success.
Notably, fallback did NOT loop — policy guardrails working.
I’m watching for any sign that paid tenants get starved when free tier spikes; so far fairness looks ok.

Allison Grant: +1 on fairness. Also: please keep an eye on label cardinality for the reason codes.
I’m seeing `x-redwood-overload-reason` aligning with the standard set (edge_admission, breaker_open, runtime_queue_full, runtime_mem_pressure). No new ad-hoc strings, thank you.

Connor O'Brien: Deploy note: canary stayed on all day, no rollbacks. Next step per rollout checklist is expanding to a 3rd model in us-east tonight (after traffic dips) if SRE signs off.

Rafael Mendes: Before we expand — any “bad” signals? E.g., too aggressive shedding, customers getting 429 when they shouldn’t, Retry-After too long/short.

Sergio Costa: Only mild concern: Retry-After distribution is a bit bimodal (2s vs 10s). The 10s cases correlate with breaker-open events.
Not necessarily wrong, but we should confirm client guidance says to respect Retry-After and add jitter (avoid retry storms).

Christine Wong: The 10s is coming from the breaker cooldown default. We can tune down to 5s but that increases probe frequency (risk: oscillation). Given canary stability, I’d keep as-is for now.

Tomáš Novák: Agree. I’d rather be slightly conservative while we’re validating. The whole point is to prevent the cascade.
Also, “clear 429 w/ Retry-After” is strictly better than “hanging 504 for 30s”.

Amara Diallo: One more nuance: streaming requests.
During the spike window, some streams got rejected at admission (429) before establishing the stream — which is fine.
I didn’t see mid-stream disconnects attributed to shedding (good sign). Previously those were nasty.

Incident Bot: Snapshot (us-east canary) @ 18:10 UTC
- breaker_open_count (5m): 3
- shed_rate_total (5m): 6.9%
- gateway_5xx_timeouts (5m): 0
- runtime_queue_depth_p99: 480 (cap=500)
- api_p99_latency: 1.98s

Rafael Mendes: Great. Action items:
1) Aisha/Sergio: pull a “customer impact” view — top API keys by 429 count, confirm mostly free tier + retrying clients.
2) Amara: double-check OpenAI-compat error body looks sane for 429/503 (no surprises).
3) Connor: OK to expand to the 3rd model in us-east tonight, but keep it behind the per-model flag so we can revert fast.

Aisha Bello: On it. I’ll post top offenders + user agent breakdown in this thread.

Sergio Costa: I’ll add a panel for “429 by SDK version” — if we see one client looping without jitter, we should proactively message docs/SDK folks.

Mina Haddad: +1, if we see retry loops, we should nudge Monica/Ibrahim (SDKs) to ensure default backoff honors Retry-After.

Rafael Mendes: Thanks all. Net: canary looks like it’s doing what we designed — stable shedding, better tail latency, fewer ambiguous 5xx. Keep watching for customer confusion on 429s.
